decision_gate.physical_capability: PASS; four-core can fight and surface reserve is strong.
decision_gate.command_release: HOLD; Palau defense alone is explicitly insufficient to release the fleet.
decision_gate.operational_slack: PARTIAL; carrier-air cadre is recovering rapidly but still strategically expensive to exchange.
decision_gate.motive_payoff: FAIL_FOR_BLIND_INTERCEPT; Palau is valuable, but there is no transport/landing force or detached high-value target whose destruction justifies a voluntary TF58 search duel.
decision_gate.information_quality: FAIL_FOR_STRIKE_RELEASE; HIGH theater warning but no stable <=90-minute weapon-quality carrier/TG track.
decision_gate.opportunity_cost: HIGH; losing strike leaders or decks before five-carrier integration would erase the benefit of the March recovery window.

decision: NO-GO FOR EASTWARD CARRIER SORTIE. Raise readiness, protect tanker/egress plans, keep the four-core mobile/concealed on the southern reaction axis, and let Palau absorb the raid.
actions: Four-core shifts to high readiness and sea-training/covered dispersal as necessary, but does not race east toward Palau.
Submarines/long-range reconnaissance continue to seek a damaged, detached or refueling US subgroup during withdrawal.
Taiho continues southward integration; its presence does not reopen the gate before five-deck synchronization.
Heavy surface ships do not make a daylight run toward a fast-carrier force.
reopen_conditions: fresh <=90-minute multi-source track on a separated/refueling/damaged US subgroup
confirmed amphibious/transport geometry fixing US fleet position for multiple days
major US deck mission-kills creating a favorable deck ratio
credible tanker/egress plan plus preserved Japanese strike cohesion
consistency_guard: This preserves the established doctrine in DECISION_RATIONALE_VARIABLE_LEDGER_v001: do not sortie main carriers merely to save Palau/Truk.
